subject: Redline request: Reliability guardrails & crediting matrix for Northbridge
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@northbridge.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Sean O'Riley <sean.oriley@northbridge.ai>, procurement@northbridge.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA: availability floor & credit carveouts - ask

Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week — Northbridge's infra team liked the latency profile on yourDedicated offering. Legal and procurement have one remaining ask on the SLA template before we can finalize: we need an explicit monthly credit schedule tied to uptime bands, and clarity on maintenance carveouts and planned maintenance notification windows.

Two specific asks from procurement:
- Cap total monthly credits so it does not exceed 30% of monthly committed dollars (we can accept a per-month cap, not an open-ended liability).
- Allow for a defined weekly maintenance window up to 3 hours per month without credit (we'll need to schedule these in advance).

Operational ask from the SRE team (Sean):
- Can Redwood confirm P95 latency SLO for inference under our committed pool (50k requests/day)? If not, we need a fallthrough credit tied to latency breaches.

We're attaching the redline the legal team started — they proposed lowering the uptime floor from 99.95% to 99.9% with a higher monthly credit. We want to avoid open-ended credit exposure but are OK with a structured banding if it caps liability.

Can you send your recommended credit bands and an approach for maintenance carveouts by Monday? If we can align, procurement will fast-track the contract.

Best,
Elena
Director of Infrastructure
Northbridge AI

Attachments: SLA_Northbridge_Redline_v3.pdf (pdf, 145KB)
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Elena Park <elena.park@northbridge.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA: availability floor & credit carveouts - ask

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and for the redline. Appreciate Sean's latency callout; that's helpful.

High-level response:
- We can agree a capped monthly credit schedule tied to uptime bands. Our standard hosted template caps at 50% of monthly committed revenue; for Dedicated we can accept a 30% cap for the first 12 months given your committed pool size.
- Planned maintenance: we propose a ~72-hour rolling notification window for scheduled maintenance and allow up to 3 hours/month as a non-creditable maintenance allowance if scheduled at least 7 days in advance. Any unscheduled maintenance would map into the credit matrix.
- Latency SLOs: for your committed pool (50k/day, 95th percentile target), Redwood can commit to p95 inference latency <= 250ms on our Dedicated pool under normal operating conditions. For latency-related credits we suggest a simple fallthrough: if p95 > 250ms for more than 30 minutes in a calendar day and it impacts >=10% of your requests, a daily credit applies and is normalized into the monthly cap.

I've sketched a crediting matrix (attached) that:
- Defines uptime bands and corresponding percentage credits of monthly committed fees,
- Enforces a 30% monthly cap,
- Separately tracks latency-triggered credits but rolls them into the same 30% cap,
- Adds a modest exclusion for scheduled maintenance (up to 3 hours/month with notice).

Can Ben and Legal (Laura) comment on whether the 7-day notice for scheduled maintenance is acceptable and whether we need additional language around force majeure or scheduled platform upgrades? Marissa, would CS be comfortable with the operational thresholds for the latency fallthrough?

If that all looks reasonable, I can send a clean redline and a DocuSign link for sign-off early next week.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

Attachments: credit_matrix_proposal.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SLA: availability floor & credit carveouts - ask

Team — forwarding Northbridge's request and my proposal (see attached matrix). TL;DR: they want a lower uptime floor in exchange for a clearly banded credit schedule with a 30% cap. They also want explicit latency fallthrough credits.

Proposed language snippets (for legal):
- Uptime bands (monthly):
  * >= 99.95%: no credit
  * 99.9% - 99.949%: 10% of monthly committed fees
  * 99.5% - 99.899%: 25% of monthly committed fees
  * < 99.5%: 30% of monthly committed fees (cap)
- Latency credit: if p95 > 250ms for >30 continuous minutes and impacting >=10% of requests, daily credit = 3% of daily pro-rated committed fees, rolled into monthly cap.
- Scheduled maintenance: up to 3 hours/month per customer if scheduled >=7 days in advance and limited to non-peak hours; such windows are excluded from uptime calculation.

Questions for you:
- Ben: does sales accept the 30% cap for the first 12 months of committed service as a standard play for enterprise large commits?
- Laura: can legal cut the uptime band language into the Master Services Agreement without additional indemnity obligations? We should also call out force majeure and platform upgrades as exceptions.
- Marissa: ops acceptability — are the latency measurement windows and the >=10% impacted threshold operationally measurable and reasonable to pledge?

If you approve, I'll update the redline and generate a DocuSign route (Northbridge prefers procurement and one exec). I've included the draft credit_matrix_proposal.xlsx in the thread.

—Aditya

Attachments: credit_matrix_proposal.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)
From: Elena Park <elena.park@northbridge.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Sean O'Riley <sean.oriley@northbridge.ai>, procurement@northbridge.ai
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 16:39:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA: availability floor & credit carveouts - ask

Aditya — this looks good and is much clearer than the redline our legal started. Two quick notes from procurement:
1) Accept the 30% cap for 12 months on the condition we get an explicit rollback clause after 12 months if usage grows > 2x with a commensurate price review.
2) Scheduled maintenance: procurement is fine with 7 days' notice but asks that notifications be delivered to procurement@northbridge.ai and a technical contact (we'll provide a list).

Sean (SRE) confirms the p95=250ms tie-out is measurable — he'll coordinate a short runbook with your CS team on how we'll collect and agree on telemetry during the proof window.

If you can send the final redline and DocuSign link with the rollback clause included, procurement will aim to sign within 48 hours.

Best,
Elena
